content:
The image shows an open soybean pod held in hand. Key observations:

- **Pod interior**: White, cottony/fluffy mycelial growth lining the inside of the pod wall
- **Seeds**: Two green beans present, appearing somewhat underdeveloped
- **Pod wall**: Brown discoloration with what appears to be fungal tissue
- **Background**: Yellow/senescing foliage visible

The white cottony fungal growth inside the pod is the most diagnostic feature. This matches White Mold (Sclerotinia stem rot) very closely — the description states "pods contain smaller, lighter, cottony seeds" and infected pods show white fluffy mycelial growth. The cottony white material lining the pod interior is characteristic of Sclerotinia/White Mold infection.
